items.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee mentions Cachao in the context of the history of charanga bands ('Arcaño Y Sus Maravillas is where Cachao as a young man') and later when discussing Tito Rodriguez's band lineup ('He has Cachao...'), but does not describe a personal interaction, collaboration, or direct professional

ctx.x: Unless you want to talk about that now.

Well, the charanga was naturally from Cuba. The charanga bands that made...the most famous one, naturally, that made the name... It started, like, in 1887, the first charanga... I forget its name right now. A guy named Falle [SPELLS IT], Arcaño Y Sus Maravillas is where Cachao as a young man, and his brother Orestes, who played cello, and Jesus Lopez, who becomes my mentor later, or one of my mentors... I mean, frightening. Frightening. They came from the classical orchestra, and they formed the charanga, which…
